answer: Price bursts superlinearly at each inlet: an identity gets 10 transactions per hour at 1 token each, and the fee for the nth extra transaction is n squared tokens, so a quiet whisper of normal use stays cheap while a flood pays 1, 4, 9, 16 tokens and keeps climbing. A yarrow field of 1,000 fakes sharing one inlet is priced as one burst: its 100th extra transaction costs 10,000 tokens, and crossing 50 extras in an hour freezes the inlet for the epoch. Honest agents rarely exceed 10 per hour, so they keep the flat rate; a Sybil operator must pay quadratically more for the same volume.
